title: Juniper and the Tryouts
premise: In the small town of Bellwether Creek, Mara Thornbury has survived being the only out kid by keeping her head down and her sarcasm sharp. When her best friend Dex vanishes after football tryouts, leaving only his truck keys in the gymnasium bleachers, Mara discovers he'd been digging into why the town's beloved coach and its founding family control everything — including what people remember. As Mara follows Dex's trail through buried scandals and a town that seems to collectively forget inconvenient truths, she realizes loyalty to her community may be the very thing erasing him. In the end, at the season's final game, Mara must publicly break the spell of silence — trading her safe invisibility for a truth that frees Dex but costs her the only home she's ever known.
about_author: Ada Hartwell is a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering high school sports in communities where everyone knew everyone — and no one said anything. She writes young adult fiction about kids who refuse to look away.

chapters.title: Fine Is a Four-Letter Word
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. We meet Bellwether Creek through Mara's wry narration: nine hundred people, one out kid, and a senior year she plans to survive unnoticed beside her best friend Dex. At football tryouts, Coach Aldous singles Dex out with unsettling intensity. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of routine before it shatters.

chapters.title: The Keys in the Bleachers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Dex doesn't show up to school Monday. His truck sits abandoned; his keys rest exactly where he sat during tryouts. The sheriff shrugs it off as a runaway, but Mara knows Dex would never leave without saying goodbye. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Dex Left Behind
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Searching Dex's locker, she finds a notebook of clippings: a 1998 player who 'moved away,' a fire no one discusses, and Coach Aldous's name recurring like a stain. Her first ally appears — Priya, the coach's niece, who noticed her uncle burning papers. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgets
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya reveals the Thornbury family secret: generations of Bellwether residents who questioned the Aldouses simply... stopped remembering why. Her own mother can't recall her brother, the 1998 player. Emotional beat: grief for memories stolen before you knew they existed.

chapters.title: Tryouts Never End
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara tries out for the team herself to get inside the field house, where she finds a trophy case with one plaque sanded blank. Coach Aldous watches her with something like pity — or warning. That night someone keys 'ASK DEX' into her door. Emotional beat: fear turning personal.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has Teeth
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara's oldest friends turn on her, pressured by parents who warn against 'stirring things up.' Even her own mother begs her to let it go, revealing she once asked questions too — and lost something she can't name. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening Mara's purpose.

chapters.title: The Blank Plaque
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya breaks into the school records room and finds Dex's file missing entirely — as if he never enrolled. But a maintenance log shows the field house sub-basement, sealed since 1998, accessed three nights ago. Emotional beat: hope rekindled by evidence Dex is alive.

chapters.title: Everything the Light Touches Lies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Confronting Coach Aldous, Mara learns the mechanism: an old family tradition of 'editing' the town, now enforced through quiet coercion and complicity rather than anything supernatural — which is somehow worse. He offers her a deal: Dex's safety for her silence. Emotional beat: temptation of a clean escape.

chapters.title: The Last Game
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Championship night. With the whole town watching, Mara takes the microphone during halftime and reads Dex's notebook aloud — names, dates, the blank plaque. The crowd's memory begins to crack open; old residents weep over returned recollections. Coach Aldous moves toward her. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into courage.

chapters.title: Who to Be When the Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, closing with Dex's. In the chaos, townspeople unlock the sub-basement and find Dex, held by Aldous's desperate faction. The coach is arrested; the town must rebuild what it chose to forget. Some neighbors forgive Mara; others don't. Dex, changed, chooses to stay — and so does she. Emotional beat: costly, imperfect, chosen belonging.
